book.dndclasses.class_guidebook.no_class: You haven't picked a class yet. Pick one in the class menu; this book will then explain yours. Until then, here is every class.

role.dndclasses.support.description: Supports make everyone around them better with buffs, songs and debuffs.
role.dndclasses.utility.description: Utility classes solve the problems swords can't: gear, scouting, obstacles and odd tricks.

dialogue.dndclasses.handed_in: You see to your quest business.
dialogue.dndclasses.greeting.unfriendly: "What do you want? Make it quick."
dialogue.dndclasses.greeting.honored: "%s! Always a pleasure. What can I do for you?"
dialogue.dndclasses.greeting.exalted: "%s, friend of our people! Anything you need."
dialogue.dndclasses.innkeeper.greeting.u: "You again. Keep your boots off the tables."
dialogue.dndclasses.innkeeper.greeting.n: "Welcome to the Green Dragon! Pull up a stool. There's ale, and there's trouble, if you're the sort that goes looking."
dialogue.dndclasses.innkeeper.greeting.f: "Ah, a friendly face! Your usual? And I've news, if you've the time."
dialogue.dndclasses.innkeeper.greeting.h: "There's always a seat by the fire for you, friend. What'll it be?"
dialogue.dndclasses.innkeeper.greeting.e: "The hero of the Shire, in my humble inn! Drinks are on the house tonight!"
dialogue.dndclasses.innkeeper.advance: Times are hard on the road. How about something up front?
dialogue.dndclasses.innkeeper.advance.ye: "Oh, very well. Three emeralds now, and don't drink them all at once."
dialogue.dndclasses.innkeeper.advance.no: "Nice try. You'll be paid when the job's done, same as everyone."
dialogue.dndclasses.innkeeper.goblins.li: "They come down the east road after dark, in twos and threes. Six of them dead and the carters might sleep easy again."
"You stand before the Mountain's King. Watch your tongue."
"A surface-dweller in my halls. Speak, and be brief."
"Welcome, friend of the Mountain. The forges burn warm for you."
"Ah, our honoured guest! Sit, sit. The ale is dark and the news is grim."
"Shield-sibling! The Mountain remembers its friends. Ask, and it is yours."
dialogue.dndclasses.hobbit_elder.greetin: "Hmph. The Shire has a long memory, and you're in it."
"Good morning! Or is it? The Thain hears of everything in these parts, sooner or later."
"Ah, the one everyone's been talking about! Sit, have a seed-cake."
"A friend of the Shire is a friend of mine. What news?"
"Our champion! There'll be a song about you yet, mark my words."

quest.dndclasses.goblin_menace.title: The Goblin Menace
quest.dndclasses.goblin_menace.1.title: Trouble on the Road
quest.dndclasses.goblin_menace.1.descrip: Goblins have been waylaying travellers on the roads to the Green Dragon. The innkeeper wants them gone.
quest.dndclasses.goblin_menace.1.stage.1: Thin out the goblins on the roads: six should send a message.
a rare magic item from the King's armoury
item.dndclasses.goblin_war_orders.toolti: Crude orders in goblin script, sealed in red wax. They speak of "the Warlord in the burning fortress" and of dwarven gold.
item.dndclasses.cursed_bone.tooltip: Cold to the touch, and etched with tiny runes that seem to whisper.
item.dndclasses.quest_lead.tooltip: A scrap of gossip torn from a bounty board.
item.dndclasses.quest_lead.stale: The trail has gone cold: nobody tells this story any more.
bounty.dndclasses.board.rumour: [%s] A Rumour: someone's heard something. Take it to find out what.
bounty.dndclasses.rumour.hint: Right-click the Rumour to follow it.
bounty.dndclasses.rumour.nothing: The rumour makes no sense to you yet. Leave it for someone else.
quest.dndclasses.goblin_menace.2.title: The Warlord's Trail
quest.dndclasses.goblin_menace.2.descrip: The goblins on the road come from a camp out in the wilds. Find it, see what they're planning, and follow the trail to whoever gives the orders.
quest.dndclasses.goblin_menace.2.no_camp: "Nobody's found their camp yet. Follow the goblins home, they always go back to it."
quest.dndclasses.goblin_menace.2.no_fort: Nobody knows where the dwarves have their halls. Look for a fortress among the mountains.
quest.dndclasses.goblin_menace.2.stage.1: Follow the map to the goblin camp and put three of its goblins down.
quest.dndclasses.goblin_menace.2.objecti: Slay goblins in a goblin camp
quest.dndclasses.goblin_menace.2.narrate: Among the dead goblin's things: sealed orders, and a crude drawing of a dwarven gate.
quest.dndclasses.goblin_menace.2.stage.2: The orders mention dwarven gold. Take them to the Dwarf King in his fortress.
quest.dndclasses.goblin_menace.2.objecti: Give the War Orders to the Dwarf King
quest.dndclasses.goblin_menace.2.stage.3: The King has read the orders. Talk him into standing with the Shire.
quest.dndclasses.goblin_menace.2.stage.4: The King will help, for a price: eight gold ingots for the Mountain's treasury.
quest.dndclasses.goblin_menace.2.objecti: Pay the King's tribute in gold ingots
quest.dndclasses.goblin_menace.2.stage.5: The orders came from a Goblin Warlord. Find one, in a Nether fortress or a war camp, and end it. Then tell the innkeeper.
quest.dndclasses.goblin_menace.2.narrate: The Warlord falls, and its war drums fall silent. The innkeeper will want to hear of this.
"A camp out in the wilds, the carters say. Here, I marked it on a map for you. Mind the spikes."
dialogue.dndclasses.goblin_menace.warlor: "A Warlord, they call it. Big brute with a war drum. They hole up in the burning fortresses of the Nether, and some lead war camps of their own."
dialogue.dndclasses.goblin_menace.plea: These orders threaten your halls as much as our fields. Stand with us.
dialogue.dndclasses.goblin_menace.blessi: "Hah! You've a tongue of silver. Very well: you have the Mountain's blessing. Our axes march with you."
dialogue.dndclasses.goblin_menace.tribut: "The Mountain does not fight for free, surface-dweller. Eight gold ingots for the treasury, and my axes are yours."
quest.dndclasses.whispering_library.1.de: The dead don't rest easy of late, and the Thain wants to know why. Bring him what they carry.
quest.dndclasses.whispering_library.1.no: The bones point somewhere far below, too far to map. Follow the eyes of ender to a stronghold, or seek out a Crypt.
quest.dndclasses.whispering_library.1.st: Put the restless dead back in the ground and gather the cursed bones some of them carry. Bring three to the Thain.
quest.dndclasses.whispering_library.1.ob: Bring Cursed Bones to the Thain
quest.dndclasses.whispering_library.1.st: The runes on the bones mean something. Read them with the Thain.
quest.dndclasses.whispering_library.1.ob: Read the runes on the bones
quest.dndclasses.whispering_library.1.st: The runes speak of a jar that holds a soul, hidden where the Lich keeps its court: a library deep in a stronghold, or the reliquary of a Crypt. Find one and smash the jar.
quest.dndclasses.whispering_library.1.ob: Find a stronghold or a Crypt
quest.dndclasses.whispering_library.1.na: The phylactery shatters. Somewhere in the dark, something screams.
quest.dndclasses.whispering_library.1.st: With its soul jar broken, the Lich can die for good. Destroy it, then tell the Thain.
quest.dndclasses.whispering_library.1.na: The Lich crumbles to dust, and this time nothing gathers it back. The whispering stops.
dialogue.dndclasses.whispering_library.b: "Old magic, and bad. The dead carry them like a mark. Bring me three and we'll see what they have to say."
dialogue.dndclasses.whispering_library.r: "Yes... a jar with a soul in it, kept under the earth: in a buried library, or in a crypt's reliquary. I've marked the nearest on your map. And take these: they'll lead you true."
"Gibberish to me, and to you, it seems. All I can tell you is these eyes of ender pull towards something. Follow the eyes, or try the old crypts, where the dead are thickest."
dialogue.dndclasses.whispering_library.l: What do I do about the Lich?
"Its jar is broken, so when it falls, it stays fallen. Go on, before it finds another way."
quest.dndclasses.ice_and_storm.title: Ice and Storm
quest.dndclasses.ice_and_storm.1.title: Ice and Storm
quest.dndclasses.ice_and_storm.1.descrip: A dwarven expedition went up into the frozen peaks and never came back. The King wants to know what became of them.
quest.dndclasses.ice_and_storm.1.no_lair: "Our scouts have lost the trail. Search the Frozen Peaks, high up."
quest.dndclasses.ice_and_storm.1.no_peak: "The storm moves about. Look to the highest mountain summits."
quest.dndclasses.ice_and_storm.1.stage.1: Find where the expedition went: a lair high on the Frozen Peaks.
quest.dndclasses.ice_and_storm.1.narrate: Frozen picks, shattered shields, and claw marks as long as your arm. The expedition met a drake.
quest.dndclasses.ice_and_storm.1.stage.2: Slay the Frost Drake and show the King a trophy from its hoard.
quest.dndclasses.ice_and_storm.1.objecti: Show the King a Frost Drake trophy
quest.dndclasses.ice_and_storm.1.narrate: "Well struck! But there's thunder on the peaks too. Something else nests up there."
quest.dndclasses.ice_and_storm.1.stage.3: A storm dragon nests on the mountain summits. Bring it down, then return to the King.
dialogue.dndclasses.ice_and_storm.expedi: "Up into the ice, after the old veins of blue. Here, our cartographers marked their route."
"Blue ice from its nest, or the staff it guards. Something to show the court the beast is dead."
"On the highest summit, where the lightning never stops. Here. Go armed."
quest.dndclasses.eye_below.title: The Eye Below
quest.dndclasses.eye_below.1.title: The Eye Below
quest.dndclasses.eye_below.1.description: Miners have gone silent in the deep. The King will say only that something down there is watching.
quest.dndclasses.eye_below.1.no_lair: "The deep roads twist too far for any map. It lies far below, in a great cavern."
quest.dndclasses.eye_below.1.stage.1: The King is hiding something about the silent miners. Hear him out.
quest.dndclasses.eye_below.1.stage.2: Something with many eyes lairs in a cavern deep below. Slay the Beholder, then return to the King.
quest.dndclasses.eye_below.1.narrate.beh: The great eye dims and closes for the last time. The deep is quiet again.
dialogue.dndclasses.eye_below.truth: Your miners didn't just go silent, did they?
dialogue.dndclasses.eye_below.truth.line: "...No. My own crews broke into its cavern, chasing gold. Keep it from the court, and the Mountain will remember. Here is the way."
dialogue.dndclasses.eye_below.lie.lines: "A cave-in, nothing more. But something down there is watching. Here is the way."
dialogue.dndclasses.eye_below.where.line: "Far below. I've marked what we know. Mind its gaze: magic dies in it."

puzzle.dndclasses.book.intro.crypt: Here the honoured dead keep their watch. Four wardens stand in the corners of this hall, and each must show the sign painted behind it, or the way stays shut.
puzzle.dndclasses.book.intro.goblin_warr: Big boss say: four rocks in corners. Turn rocks so they show picture on wall behind. Wrong picture, hot floor! Ha!
puzzle.dndclasses.book.intro.dwarven_rui: By order of the Hold: four rune-wardens guard this gate. Set each to the sign carved on the walls of its corner, and the seal will lift.
puzzle.dndclasses.book.rules:
Turn a rune with your hand. Set all four together, and the vents will judge you.

Where a corner's walls are bare and black, that warden takes any sign.

One corner's sign was hacked away. Read on.
puzzle.dndclasses.riddle.sun:
The hacked-away sign:

I rise each morning and die each dusk, and still the dead fear only me.
puzzle.dndclasses.riddle.moon:
The hacked-away sign:

I wax and wane but never eat; I keep the night watch and borrow my light.
puzzle.dndclasses.riddle.eye:
The hacked-away sign:

I see all yet never weep for what I see; close me and the world is gone.
puzzle.dndclasses.riddle.flame:
The hacked-away sign:

Feed me and I live, give me drink and I die.
puzzle.dndclasses.riddle.crown:
The hacked-away sign:

Kings wear me, yet I have never had a head of my own.
puzzle.dndclasses.riddle.skull:
The hacked-away sign:

Every one of you carries me, but I am only shown when you are done.

dialogue.dndclasses.dragonborn_elder.gre: "The ancestors watch you, outsider. So do I."
"Welcome to the Shrine of the Three Breaths. Mind the altars."
"Friend of the temple. The fires burn warm for you."
"You honour our ancestors. Sit, and tell me of the lairs you have seen."
"Clutch-kin in all but blood! Ask, and the temple answers."
